paragraphs.text: A loose [red tea](red:definition) from Yunnan, finished in the sun. Its last drying was done in sunlight rather than over heat, which makes it a [sun-dried red](dian-hong:old-tree-and-sun-dried). That is a choice of process, not a separate kind of tea.

Up to that final step the leaf was [made as every red tea is](dian-hong:making): withered, rolled to break its cells, then left to oxidise fully until it turned from green to reddish brown. Yunnan's own red, [Dian Hong](dian-hong:definition), began with a trial batch Feng Shaoqiu made in Shunning, now Fengqing, in late 1938. The trade still does not agree whether a red dried in the sun belongs under that name.

brewing.text: Dian Hong takes hot water, roughly 90 to 100°C. A common start is about 5 grams to 100 ml, with short steeps that lengthen slowly as the leaf opens.

notice.text: A full, sweet cup, often described as malty, with chocolate or cocoa and honey notes and sometimes something floral. The liquor runs golden to bright red, and a good grade has little bitterness.
